newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy June industrial output seen flat- employers.
newsitem.headline: Italy June industrial output seen flat- employers.

text.p: Italian industrial production was expected to be basically flat in June, but sales and orders rose strongly, Italian employers' federation Confindustria said in a regular survey published on Thursday.
Output was expected to dip an adjusted 0.3 percent in June month-on-month after a 0.7 percent increase in May.

However, on a year-on-year basis, industrial production was seen rising 0.5 percent this month, taking into account the fact that there are 21 working days in June compared with 20 in the same period last year.
On an unadjusted basis, output was forecast to climb 4.5 percent year-on-year against a 1.1 percent drop in May, Confindustria said.
Industrial output rose 1.1 percent in the first six months of the year compared with the same period last year.
New orders were seen growing 2.7 percent year-on-year in June from a 3.3 percent increase in May, while turnover and sales were up 3.8 percent against a previous 1.8 percent rise.
Sales and turnover on the domestic market were up 5.2 percent while those abroad rose 2.0 percent, Confindustria said.
It added that the mechanical/electrical sector, excluding transport production, saw a negative month in June, in terms of production, sales and new orders.
By contrast the transport sector registered a "very favourable" period in June.
